theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the headline theme and the only high-score leader that is simultaneously eligible (passes the absolute-trend gate), durable (0.8), fully broad (breadth 1.0), trend-tagged (hurst 'trend'), and not crowded. The eligibility gate is the one validated edge (drawdown control), and Banks passes it cleanly while the raw scoreboard leader (Oil & Gas) does not.
theses.dissent: Big Banks has not actually led the scoreboard (rank 2, not 1); its momentum score is below Oil & Gas, and cross-sectional momentum rank has ~no forward IC in this market — so there is no return-forecast case, only a staying-power/drawdown case.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO closes below its 50-day moving average and stays there for 5 consecutive sessions before the check-by date

theses.subject: Utilities & Renewables
theses.thesis: Utilities & Renewables is an eligible trend (eligibility true, durability 0.8, hurst 'trend') with broad participation (breadth 0.917) and negative crowding (z -0.24, nowhere near crowded). It is the defensive/rate-sensitive bookend to Banks — both are eligible, durable, trend-tagged themes, and the gate's only validated edge is drawdown avoidance, which these two share.
theses.dissent: Its momentum score is only mid-table (0.365), well below Banks and Consumer Staples, and utilities are highly rate-sensitive — a macro rates shock in either direction could unwind the trend leg that the gate is currently reading as healthy.

falsifier.text: XUT.TO underperforms ZEB.TO by 4% or more over any 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Technology
theses.thesis: Technology is eligible but crowded (z 1.25, crowded: true) and carries a negative momentum score (-0.233) with a 'mixed' hurst tag — no clean trend. Crowding is a size-down/avoid caution only, never a fade, but combined with negative score and mixed trend-health it argues for standing aside rather than owning this name while the crowding flag is up.
theses.dissent: The absolute-trend gate (the one validated edge) still passes Technology — so the drawdown-control discipline would not itself exclude it, and avoiding an eligible name purely on crowding risks abandoning the only proven rule for a coincident flag.
